channel.title: Zig Guide Live
channel.description: A Zig tutorial and cookbook where every snippet is compiled and run against current Zig master on every build, and runs in your browser as WebAssembly.

item.title: Hello World
item.description: Your first Zig program, and why main now takes an argument.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Binary Files
item.description: A small binary format with a header, written one field at a time, and a reader that checks every byte it did not write.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Reading CSV
item.description: A CSV reader as a four-state machine, with a trace of every byte, the cases splitting on commas gets wrong, and errors with line numbers.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Writing CSV
item.description: Quote a field only when it needs it, double the quotes inside it, and prove the writer by reading its output back.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Directories
item.description: Create a tree of directories, list one level, walk every level, rename a directory and delete the whole tree.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: When Things Go Wrong
item.description: What stat tells us, six file operations that fail and the error each one names, messages a person can act on, and cleaning up a half-written file.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Open, Read, Close
item.description: Three ways to read a file, and what each one does when the file is bigger than you planned for.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Random Access
item.description: A file of fixed-size records. Read record N without reading the ones before it, change one in place, and grow and shrink the file.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Reading Line by Line
item.description: A line loop over a file, the three line endings it meets, a line longer than the buffer, and a large file through a small buffer.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Writing Text Files
item.description: Truncate or keep, create only if new, append, the flush that was forgotten, and replacing a file in one step.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Filesystem
item.description: Every disk operation now takes an Io.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Writing an Image File
item.description: PPM, the image format you can write without a library, and the one strict rule that is easy to break.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Binary Search
item.description: The half-open window, the invariant that keeps it correct, and the two bounds std already ships.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: The Monotonic Stack
item.description: A stack of the indices still waiting for an answer, and the two counters that show the inner loop keeps the total linear.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Sliding Window
item.description: One addition and one subtraction instead of a fresh sum, the window that grows and shrinks, and the count that shows the inner loop keeps the total linear.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: A Batch Job Runner
item.description: Four workers, one batch, three kinds of shared state, and a measurement that says one thread did all of it.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: A Hash Map from Scratch
item.description: Open addressing with linear probing, growth at 75%, and the tombstone, which looks like a hack but is what makes delete work.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Antialiasing
item.description: Coverage is alpha. Sample the inside test sixteen times per pixel and the jagged edges go away.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: A Bar Chart
item.description: Turning numbers into pixels is one division, and getting it wrong misleads the reader.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Histograms and Levels
item.description: Count what the image contains, and the lookup table that fixes it comes straight from the counts. Auto-levels, equalization, and why you apply them to luma.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Per-Pixel Transforms
item.description: Brightness, contrast, threshold and invert are all one table lookup, and brightness needs Zig's saturating add.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: If Expressions
item.description: No truthiness: if takes a bool.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Optionals
item.description: Zig's answer to null, checked by the compiler.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Pointer Sized Integers
item.description: usize, isize, and why they are not the same as u64.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: A Type Function as the Front Door
item.description: The central pattern of a Zig library: take the caller's type, return a richer one.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Exiting
item.description: exit is the process stopping, not your program returning.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Signals
item.description: A handler interrupts you between two instructions. Set a flag and return.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: The Io Interface
item.description: Anything that can block takes an Io; the caller picks how.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Readers and Writers
item.description: The buffered Reader and Writer interfaces introduced in Zig 0.15.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Strings
item.description: Search, trim, split, join. All of it lives in std.mem.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: An Index Over the Log
item.description: A second structure, derived from the first, that you now have to keep in sync.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Talking to the Operating System
item.description: Your program is handed streams it did not open, and must return a status.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: String Primitives
item.description: strlen, compare, copy and trim, written out. This is where the off-by-one error happens.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: A Tree-Walking Interpreter
item.description: Evaluate a node by evaluating its children.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: A Virtual Machine
item.description: Fetch, decode, execute. A loop over an array, with no tree.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Slugs Are Arithmetic
item.description: Base62 over the row id, and the validation a redirect service needs.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: File Uploads
item.description: A format where the client picks the delimiter, and a filename you cannot trust until you check it.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: A Template Engine
item.description: Substitution is the easy half. Escaping by default is the harder half.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: C Pointers
item.description: [*c]T: the pointer type translate-c emits, and why to convert it at the boundary.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Cross-compilation
item.description: Every target, out of the box.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Dependencies
item.description: Declaring, fetching, and wiring a package with build.zig.zon.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Emitting an Executable
item.description: Building without a build.zig.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: A Contest Template
item.description: The one program in the section that reads real stdin, and the three things a judge punishes that a browser never shows.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Take or Skip: The 0/1 Knapsack
item.description: Every subset, then the take-or-skip recursion, the table that stops it repeating itself, the walk back to the chosen items, and the one-row version whose loop direction decides the answer.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Union-Find (Disjoint Set Union)
item.description: Groups that merge as edges arrive, from a parent array where a merge moves one root and a find walks to it.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Async, Future and Group
item.description: async, Future, and Group, all through the Io interface.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Choosing an Io
item.description: Threaded, the evented implementations, and building one yourself.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Locks and Semaphores
item.description: RwLock, Semaphore and Condition, past the point where a Mutex is enough.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Queues
item.description: Io.Queue as a bounded channel between tasks, with close and back pressure.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Pillai

item.title: Select
item.description: Waiting for whichever task finishes first, and cancelling the rest.
